text:
Michael DiPietro waited a long time for this. Drafted by Vancouver in 2017, he played one NHL game last season, and now he is one of the more surprising stories in Boston. Through six games he is 4-1-0 with a .924 save rate and has saved 4.9 goals above expected, meaning he kept out 4.9 more goals than the shots he faced would usually allow. That's 91st percentile among goalies.

The standout number is on the hardest chances: .842 on high-danger shots against a league .685. He also posted a shutout against Nashville on Oct. 22. Six games is a tiny sample, though, and his low-danger save rate (.953) is a little below league average, so we'd hold off on big conclusions. The Boston Globe wrote about him and his old AHL teammate Brandon Bussi both shining in the NHL this fall, and NDTV Sports asked whether his start "could change everything" for the Bruins. For now he's a backup who has made the most of every chance.
